test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements about magnetic fields:

(a) The relative strength of a magnetic field is shown by the degree of closeness of lines.

(b) Magnetic field lines have magnitudes only and no directions.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (a).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The statement (a) is **correct**.

 
 
• The degree of **closeness of magnetic field line**s indicates the **strength **of the magnetic field.
 
• The closer the lines, the **stronger **the magnetic field.
 
 
 
• The statement (b) is **incorrect.**
 
 
• Magnetic field lines **not only have magnitudes** but also have directions.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field is indicated by the **direction of the lines,** which always point from the **north pole to the south pole.**
 
 
 
• Magnetic fields are areas around magnets or moving electric charges where a **magnetic force **can be observed.
 
• The strength of a magnetic field is measured in units of **tesla (T) or gauss (G).**
 
• The direction of the magnetic field can be determined by using a** compass**.
 
• The** north end **of the compass needle points towards the **south pole **of the magnet, and vice versa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Magnetic field lines are those in a magnetic field whose density indicates the field's size and whose tangent at any given place indicates the field's direction.
 
• They form **closed loops**.
 
• Magnetic field lines do not intersect with each other as it would mean that the direction of the magnetic field at that point would be undefined.
